objet: The French assets, and what I propose to do about them
disponibilite: I remain available to answer any question on these terms.

corps.p: Your message raised a second matter, quite separate from the Valais tax line. Inheritance tax paid out of your father's estate on assets situated in France which were never received, and an apartment in Neuilly-sur-Seine whose fate you do not know. That is a different estate in a different country, and it needs its own mandate.
I propose to take it on. The question to answer is what your father was entitled to receive in France, what became of it, and what remains open to you today.

One step can be taken almost at once, and it is the one that will tell us the most. A request to the French land registry gives the present owner of the Neuilly apartment and every transfer of title since. It is open to any person, without having to prove one's capacity as an heir, so it does not wait for a certificate of succession. Alongside it, the register of wills, the identity of the notary who administered the estate, the declaration of estate itself, and the bank and life assurance registers.
For this, EUR 3,500 excluding tax per month, alongside the Swiss mandate.

I also propose to move the whole engagement to euros at par. What we agreed at CHF 7,500 becomes EUR 7,500. At today's European Central Bank rate, EUR 1 buys CHF 0.938, so that figure is worth EUR 7,996. You therefore pay some EUR 500 a month less than you accepted, and you carry no currency risk on a file denominated in Swiss francs. The total is EUR 11,000 excluding tax per month.

Either side may be ended at the end of any month, and at the end of the second month we review scope and fee together. Should the French searches come back empty, you stop paying for them. A result fee of 10% excluding tax applies to what is actually recovered, and only to that.
Confirm and I will send you the two engagement letters.

Two things are still outstanding, and the first is urgent. The date on which you first learned of the CHF 302,870 balance, and how. And who signed the settlement agreement of 12 February 2025, and on what date, since your father died during its negotiation.
